newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama Canal to use relay system during overhaul.
newsitem.headline: Panama Canal to use relay system during overhaul.

text.p: The Panama Canal Commission on Monday said it was carrying out 24-hour vessel relay operations to reduce delays while maintenance work was being carried out at the canal's Gatun and Miraflores locks.

"The Gatun east lane and Miraflores west lane are temporarily closed while workers carry out tow-track rehabilitation, miter gate overhaul and other inspection, cleaning and repair projects," the commission said in a statement.

The commission is conducting 24-hour relay operations in the lanes opposite the outages to keep transit delays to a minimum, it said. Relay operations increase the number of ships that can travel in a single lane by using towing locomotives to pass a vessel more quickly from one set of locks to another.
The maintenance and improvement project will require the closing of one lane of ship traffic at Miraflores until July 19 and at Gatun until July 16.
The commission said 27 vessels were scheduled to travel though the canal Monday.

"Just after midnight July 14, 47 ships were awaiting transit of the waterway, with 13 of those not ready for scheduling," the commission said. Some 43 vessels were expected to arrive at the canal on Monday, with 32 arrivals expected Tuesday.
The average Canal Waters Time (CWT) -- the period that a vessel spends between its arrival and completed transit of the waterway -- was 43.7 hours on July 13.
(( -- Paul de Bendern, Panama City newsroom, 507-223 7739))
